key_insight: This paper proposes COSA-GS, a practical compression approach for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reduces storage without relying on expensive spatial context modeling. It also improves reliability by avoiding floating-point context inference issues that can break entropy decoding across platforms.
problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting offers high-quality novel-view synthesis, but its large storage footprint makes deployment difficult. Existing compression methods are often too complex and can be numerically unstable across hardware/software environments, leading to decoding failures.
method: Builds context without depending on irregular 3D spatial aggregation, simplifying the compression pipeline.
Avoids floating-point context inference to reduce platform-specific numerical inconsistency.
Targets practical entropy coding that is more robust and easier to train/deploy than prior methods.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it makes 3DGS more deployable in real systems where memory, bandwidth, and cross-platform reliability are important. It can help bring high-quality 3D scene representations closer to practical use in robotics, AR/VR, and graphics applications.
